title: Monotheism as re-description of the plural Elohim
statement: The Hebrew Bible preserves a divine council and plural divine beings alongside its demands for exclusive allegiance, and the anti-idol polemic of the prophetic traditions functions less as an arithmetic claim about how many superhuman beings exist than as a struggle over memory, representation, mediation, and loyalty; the corpus's stronger proposal reads prophetic monotheism as a progressive re-description of the plural Elohim into one immaterial God — so that the monotheism/polytheism division is the wrong question to put to the sources.

includes: The textual layer, which is substantially mainstream: council and plurality texts (Psalm 82; Deuteronomy 32:8-9; 1 Kings 22) alongside exclusive-allegiance texts, and the scholarly account of monotheism as a development (Smith)

The functional reading of anti-idol polemic: memory, representation, mediation, and loyalty rather than arithmetic — including the cross-tradition instances the article assembles (Paul's 'many gods and many lords'; the Qur'an's rebuke of intercession by people who already acknowledge the creator)

The corpus's stronger proposal, which is speculative: the progressive re-description of the plural Elohim into one abstract God, with the canon's own observation of the singular-God translation (woh-claim-0009) as its hinge
Preservation of irreducible differences among the traditions compared; the reading does not flatten Israel, Paul, and the Qur'an into one theology
excludes: Any claim that the biblical authors secretly intended plural reference; the re-description is read as a historical development, not a conspiracy
A general theory of monotheism beyond the traditions the corpus has actually worked through
The historicity of the Elohim, which is woh-claim-0001's burden
Denial of the mainstream developmental account; the corpus reading sits on top of it, adding a referent claim the mainstream account does not make

source_references.locator: Chapter 3, paragraph 4 (humanity worships stone and idols after forgetting its creators); Chapter 5, paragraph 21 (Elohim/Eloha and the singular-God translation)
PSA-82 (the council and the sentence on the elohim)
Deuteronomy 32:8-9 (the apportionment of the nations; the benei elohim reading attested at Qumran)
The intercession-rebuke passages the article reads (acknowledging the creator while approaching through intermediaries)
Mark S. Smith's developmental account of Israelite religion — the mainstream floor under the corpus's stronger proposal
The academic treatment of the Raelian reinterpretation of biblical divinity

alternatives.statement: The mainstream developmental account fully explains the plural traces and the polemic; no remembered plural referent is needed on top of it.
The functional reading of the polemic is itself just mainstream scholarship restated; the corpus adds a referent without adding explanation.
Reading Israel, Paul, and the Qur'an through one re-description narrative flattens traditions whose theologies of divine plurality are irreducibly different.
Re-describing theological development as memory-loss about real beings re-describes religion in a technological idiom without explaining anything the developmental account does not.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0009 is revised or retired.
The reading fails to predict any textual particular that the developmental account does not.
Comparative review shows the functional reading of the polemic does not hold for one of the traditions the article assembles, requiring a narrowing.
Public prose begins asserting authorial intent or a general theory of monotheism, which this record excludes.
